literal: The great without respecting if one behaves, by the great un-departing sorrow it will give.
translation: If one conducts oneself without respecting the great, it will bring unceasing sorrow caused by those very great ones.
modern: பெரியவர்களை மதிக்காமல் ஒருவன் நடந்துகொண்டால், அந்தப் பெரியவர்களால் அவனுக்கு ஒருபோதும் நீங்காத துன்பம் வந்து சேரும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against the danger of disrespecting people of great power or virtue. The phrase 'பேணாது ஒழுகின்' describes conducting oneself without showing due honor to such individuals. If one acts this way, it will result in 'பேரா இடும்பை', which means sorrow that does not depart or cease. The word 'பெரியாரால்' emphasizes that the great themselves, or the very act of offending them, will be the direct cause of this unending affliction.
